clue.text: Small animal for country doctor to exercise

parts.note: country as in open land or a field of farmland
MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: A rural GP is told to take a small pet out for a walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodent of meadows and hedgerows, the wood mouse, is a small wild animal.

clue.text: Such a lady was Eleanor Roosevelt

definitions.text: Such a lady was Eleanor Roosevelt

parts.words: Such a lady was Eleanor Roosevelt
parts.note: the wife of a US president holds the title that pairs this word with 'Lady'; Eleanor was wife of Franklin D Roosevelt

explanation.definitionFit: The President's wife is called the First Lady, the title Eleanor Roosevelt held from 1933 to 1945.

clue.text: One displaying evidence in court?

parts.note: suggests a lawyer producing exhibits in a trial, but means someone who shows goods or work at a show

explanation.definitionFit: Evidence produced in court is an exhibit, so one who shows things publicly, at a fair or show, is playfully the person displaying exhibits.

clue.text: Look-alikes with superb playing technique

parts.note: a person's double is a look-alike
topping is old-fashioned British slang for excellent

explanation.surface: Impersonators show off a brilliant method of performing.
explanation.walkthrough: The text as held had 'Look-alines'; the printed page reads 'Look-alikes'.
explanation.definitionFit: On a violin or cello, bowing two strings at once is a way of playing, a performance technique.

clue.text: Rise above plain, up-river

parts.note: something overt is plain to see

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for the river is written bottom to top

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: Something climbs high above a flat plain upstream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' looks like a noun (flat land) but is the adjective OVERT; 'up' turns PO into OP.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtop is to exceed in height, to tower over.

clue.text: He backs Poles in track appearance

indicators.note: the poles sit inside the word for the track

parts.note: spoor is the visible trail or track of an animal
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: A man supports Polish athletes making an appearance on a running track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland; it is the compass poles N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A backer who funds or supports a person or event is its sponsor.

clue.text: Aristocratic traveller returning to the country

indicators.note: returning means the two pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in the old U and non-U usage
a rep is a commercial traveller, a salesman

explanation.surface: A nobleman on his travels comes back to his homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses UREP to give the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American nation on the Pacific coast is a country.

clue.text: One entering old court to brood

indicators.note: entering means the numeral goes into the word for the old court

parts.note: justices in eyre were medieval circuit judges, so an eyre is an old court
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A person goes into an ancient courtroom to sit and mope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brood' looks like a verb (to mope) but is the noun: a nest's young.
explanation.definitionFit: The nest of an eagle, and also the young birds hatched in it, so a family of eaglets.

clue.text: Affected to be a simpleton working for world peace?

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, exists to keep peace between countries
a natural was an old word for a person born simple-minded

explanation.surface: Is it pretentious to be a naive soul campaigning for global harmony?
explanation.walkthrough: A 'natural' in the old sense is a born fool; the UN is the world body that seeks peace.
explanation.definitionFit: Affected manners are artificial, not the way one naturally behaves.

clue.text: Prejudice involving CID in main riots

indicators.note: involving here means twisting together, so all the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bias is alleged against detectives caught up in large-scale civil unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' is the anagram signal: its old sense is entangling. All the letters of CID IN MAIN RIOTS are rearranged; 'riots' looks like the signal but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfair treatment of people for their race or sex is bias, the same thing as prejudice.

clue.text: Provide new quarters — it's part of the army game

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
house, or housey-housey, is the army's name for bingo

explanation.surface: Billeting troops anew is just part of military life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the army game' reads as a phrase for service life; HOUSE (housey-housey) is the forces' name for bingo, the numbers game.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone new accommodation or living space is to rehouse them.

clue.text: It's oh so short, I hear, in Sophocles

definitions.text: It's oh so short, I hear, in Sophocles

parts.words: It's oh so short, I hear, in Sophocles
parts.note: a Greek letter whose name means 'little O', the short O sound, as Sophocles would have written it

explanation.definitionFit: The fifteenth Greek letter's name means small O, the short vowel as opposed to omega, the long one.

clue.text: Systematically arranges forbidden tales, perhaps

parts.note: tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, meaning forbidden

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the word tales may be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone methodically sorts out stories that are banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns TALES into LATES.
explanation.definitionFit: To set data out in rows and columns is to arrange it in a table, systematically.

clue.text: Comb the top of the wave

explanation.surface: A hairstyling instruction set at the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockscomb is a bird's crest; the foaming peak of a breaking wave is likewise its crest.

clue.text: The fruits of history, we learn?

definitions.text: The fruits of history, we learn?

parts.words: The fruits of history, we learn?
parts.note: edible palm fruits share their name with the years and days pupils memorise in history lessons

explanation.definitionFit: Palm fruits share a name with the years pupils memorise in history: 1066, 1815.

clue.text: Low ship's cook took food to some degree

parts.note: doctor is low slang, sailors' jargon, for a ship's cook
ate means took food

explanation.surface: A humble galley chef ate something to a certain extent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to some degree' looks like an adverb phrase but defines the academic degree; 'doctor' is old sailors' slang for the cook.
explanation.definitionFit: A PhD is a university qualification, the highest academic degree.

clue.text: Dish that costs humble campanologist nothing

indicators.note: costs here means the phrase loses, or pays out, the zero

parts.note: humble means poor, lowly
nothing is O, zero
a campanologist is a bell-ringer

explanation.surface: A bowl that a poor bell-ringer gets free of charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'costs ... nothing' reads as 'is free'; it means POOR RINGER loses an O.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bowl for porridge or soup is a kind of dish.

clue.text: Range out of order? Then eat this dish

indicators.note: out of order means the letters of range are jumbled

parts.note: to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: The cooker is broken, so eat this meal out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' turns RANGE into GRENA; a range is also a kitchen stove.
explanation.definitionFit: A fricandeau of veal or poultry, larded and braised, is a dish.

clue.text: Bird, bulb or busybody?

parts.note: a corm is a bulb-like underground stem
taken as written
the ant is the proverbially busy insect, a busy body

explanation.surface: A list of choices for what something might be: a bird, a bulb, a meddler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busybody' is read as busy body, the industrious ant.
explanation.definitionFit: A large black diving seabird of coasts is one kind of bird.

clue.text: Gas used after missiles in a riot

parts.note: ammo, ammunition, is missiles

indicators.note: riot means the letters of the words in a are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Tear gas follows the firing of projectiles at a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riot' rearranges IN A to NIA, which comes after AMMO.
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent compound of nitrogen and hydrogen is a gas.

clue.text: Soldier's land survey

explanation.surface: A military man's map of the terrain.
explanation.definitionFit: A Territorial Army volunteer is a soldier; a terrier was also a register or survey of land holdings.

clue.text: Conception many find perfect

parts.note: a conception is an idea
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so many

explanation.surface: A notion that numerous people consider flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conception' looks like the definition but gives IDEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal means flawless, matching a standard of perfection.

clue.text: Deck where everybody jumps, the cockneys say

indicators.note: a cockney drops the H and says the vowel of all with an R-ish drawl

parts.note: everybody means all, and jumps means hop

explanation.surface: On which floor of the ship does everyone leap, Londoners ask.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys are working-class Londoners who drop their H's: 'all hop' comes out as 'orl 'op'.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest deck of a sailing warship is a ship's deck.

clue.text: Excellent way to support Liberal land-owner

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces placed underneath support the one on top

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written AI with 1 as I
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A fine route backs a Liberal estate owner.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, top quality, is written AI here. 'to support' puts AI and RD below L.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish proprietor of a landed estate is called a laird, a land-owner.

clue.text: Mother takes Sandhurst cadet to eastern preserve

parts.note: ma is mother
RMA is the Royal Military Academy at Sandhurst
a cadet is a young man, a lad

explanation.surface: A mum takes a trainee officer to an Eastern nature reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandhurst is the British Army's officer academy, the RMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A jam made from oranges is a fruit preserve.

clue.text: Social distinction rejected in the dental centre

indicators.note: rejected means the run of letters is read backwards
in means the letters lie within the words dental centre

explanation.surface: Status is turned down at the dentist's practice.
explanation.walkthrough: The run TALCE sits inside 'dental centre'; 'rejected' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliance of success or reputation, social prestige, is a distinction.

clue.text: A city noted for trippers on the bridge?

definitions.text: A city noted for trippers on the bridge?

parts.words: A city noted for trippers on the bridge?
parts.note: trippers are dancers in the French nursery song about dancing on the bridge of a Provence city, not day-trippers

explanation.walkthrough: The French song 'Sur le pont d'...' has people dancing on the bridge there.
explanation.definitionFit: A city on the Rhône in Provence, the papal seat in the 14th century.

clue.text: First to sign

explanation.surface: A plain instruction about who signs first.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening letter is the first one; to sign with one's opening letters is to put a short signature on something.

clue.text: Journalist with daily, extremely fluid in circulation

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist

indicators.note: extremely means take the extreme, outermost letters of the word daily

explanation.surface: A reporter works for a newspaper that is very much in circulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in circulation' looks like a newspaper's sales; here it is liquid swirling round.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirlpool of water or air going round is a current of fluid circulating.

clue.text: In the RAF he could be a physicist

indicators.note: could be tells us the letters of the phrase may become something else

explanation.surface: An airman in the air force might turn out to be a scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges all the letters of IN THE RAF HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Gabriel, the German-born scientist who devised a temperature scale, was a physicist.
